text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- Bulgaria's biggest refinery Neftochim said outdated equipment caused an explosion and fire on Tuesday which stopped the refinery's production process. Nobody was killed or injured by the incident.
-- The Sofia City Court said it had postponed to September ruling on an insolvency suit against Bulgaria's First Private Bank (FPB), filed by the Bulgarian National Bank.

The court demanded an official statement on who is the bank's official representative after the term of the bank's sequestrators expired in May. FBP was placed in receivership by the central bank in May 1996.

-- Bulgaria's Military Prosecution said that recent police operations were too aggressive and police officers were poorly controlled. The office has received 51 complaints from civilians who claimed that police officers violated their rights in a raid in Sofia's Neron-2 night club last week.
-- Sofia's mayor Stefan Sofianski said he expected the long delayed start of services on the Sofia underground railway by January.
-- France's biggest private bank Societe Generale opened a branch in Sofia to service corporate clients operating in Bulgaria, Robert Frank, general manager of the branch said.

-- Bulgaria's Deputy Prime Minister Evgeni Bakardzhiev said he would leave for Moscow next week to discuss with Russian government officials transiting of Russian natural gas through Bulgaria's territory.
-- Sofia Municipal Bank said it would raise its capital to 10 billion levs from 2.4 billion levs by the end of the year.
-- Bulgaria's Special Forces policemen will have to pass lie detector tests every six months from August 1 to check their loyalty to the police, Interior Ministry secretary Bozhidar Popov said.
-- Bulgaria's budget deficit fell by 10.28 billion levs in the second half of June to 435.76 billion levs, Finance Ministry figures showed.
-- Bulgaria's Justice Minister Vasil Gotsev said he would ask for cooperation from foreign security agencies to investigate wealthy Bulgarians abroad in a move to crack down on organised crime.
